headline: GRAINS TICK HIGHER AHEAD OF STOCKS DATA AT 11 CT
lead: Corn's up a quarter-cent shy of $5.25, beans up a nickel-plus to $13.03, and none of it means much with Quarterly Grain Stocks landing at 11 CT. Nobody's positioning hard into a report that could move old-crop supply pictures either way. Every bushel priced this morning got priced without knowing what USDA knows.
teaser: Grains drift higher into Grain Stocks at 11 CT; crude holds its Iran bid at $90.38.

one_number.context: Cow slaughter is down 40% since 2022, the tightest culling rate on record, and it's the real floor under the cattle cycle, not the daily price tick.

yesterdays_call.note: Crude broke through $91 as called, settling $90.38 on Trump's no-sanctions-relief line on Iran; the down call played out clean.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called crude down toward $91.00 ($92.12 when the call was made). It closed at $90.38.

action: Nothing to do at $5.25 corn ahead of Grain Stocks; a settle above $5.29 on the data is the first reason to move.

sections.title: Grains Wait On Stocks
sections.body:
- Corn ticked up a quarter-cent to **$5.25** and beans firmed a nickel-plus to $13.03, both sitting near the top of their 52-week range with nobody willing to lean hard before 11 CT.
- Feedstuffs called it right this morning: prices mixed ahead of Wednesday's hotly anticipated USDA report, and that's exactly what the tape looks like.
sections.so_what: Positioning, not conviction; the real move waits for the report.

sections.title: Cattle Cycle Turns, Slowly
sections.body:
- Live cattle slipped 0.3% to **$217.28** while feeders firmed 0.4% to $333.77, the spread still favoring the feeder side of the trade.
- Beef Magazine's read on the cycle matters more than today's tick: cow slaughter is down 40% since 2022, a projected record-low 7.3% culling rate for 2026.
sections.so_what: The herd rebuild is the multi-year story; today's tick is noise on top of it.

sections.title: Crude Holds The Iran Bid
sections.body:
- WTI added 0.6% to **$90.38** after Trump ruled out easing Iran sanctions, the headline that's kept a floor under the barrel since Tuesday's pullback.
- JPMorgan says Middle East flows are almost fully recovered near 17.5 million barrels a day, which argues against the fear premium even as the price holds it.
sections.so_what: Supply data and fear headlines are pulling crude in opposite directions again.

outside_the_pit.title: Cow-calf profits into 2027 hinge on 7 drivers
outside_the_pit.body: CattleFax flags feed cost, packer margin, and herd rebuild pace as the levers that decide 2027 returns, worth a look before you pencil next year's budget.

watch_list.desc: Quarterly Grain Stocks; a bearish corn stocks number pressures $5.25, a tight number lifts it.
Weekly Export Sales; beans need over 1.5 MMT to hold this week's bid above $13.00.
Iran sanctions headlines; any easing talk knocks crude off its $90.38 floor fast.
